rule: No process-global mutable state in the gwz-py native layer: pass it through the session/operation context (GwzCoreSessionDesign O9). This list is the complete inventory of production exceptions. gwz-core's check_process_globals.py, run by src/tests/test_process_globals.py, fails on anything unlisted and on entries that no longer match, so the list only shrinks. 'debt', 'permanent', 'owner' and 'imposed_by' mean what the rule of gwz-core's scripts/checks/process_globals_allowlist.json says (GwzCoreSessionCrateMap §1, 'No globals').

entries.name: env::vars_os
entries.imposed_by: the process interface: a host process's environment is its own, and the extension is its driver, which captures it and passes it in (GwzCoreSessionDesign §5.6)
entries.reason: The per-operation transport's environment snapshot (1.1.0 S6.2): read once for each network operation at the native entry, in call and submit, while the caller holds the GIL, so no Python thread's os.environ write can race it; the operation's runtime then reads no process environment (gwz-py dev-docs/GwzPyPerOperationTransportDesign.md §2.3).
